It is further submitted that appellants were traumatized from the fact that their young son was sent to jail in the DV case and they are senior citizens, illiterate and appellant no. 2 is bed-ridden and they did not know the nuances of law and the certified copy was applied in 23.06.2023 and then, the present appeal was filed.

It is further submitted that the appellants should not suffer due to defective application filed by the previous counsel and prayed for condonation of delay of 126 days (4 months 4 days) as the appellants have good prima facie case in their favour in the present appeal.

It is also argued by Ld. Counsel for the appellants that Shikha Garg (respondent/complainant)
and Satish Garg were married on 22.04.2008 and have two children.
Respondent lived with father-in-law, mother-in-law, brother-in-law and sister-in- law (wife of brother-in-law) from 2008 to 2010 at Dilshad Garden, New Delhi.
Sister-in-law (husband's sister) got married in 2004 and has been living with her husband in Tri Nagar, Delhi.
In mid 2020, the respondent and her husband shifted to C-501 (Tower C), Apex Green Valley, Sector 9, Vaishali, Ghaziabad, KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT

Appellants along with the brother-in-law and sister-in-law (wife of brother-in-law) of complainant were continuously living at R-4B, Dilshad Garden, Delhi and later in 2015, they shifted to another flat in A-901 (Tower-A), Apex Green Valley, Sector 9, Vaishali, Ghaziabad, UP.

In 2021,
differences arose between the respondent and her husband resulting in Divorce proceedings being filed before Ghaziabad District Courts, which are currently pending.

4. It is further submitted that respondent and her husband lived with the appellants together only for a brief period of 2.5 years from the date of their marriage and for any alleged incident of domestic violence, there should be a subsisting domestic relationship and there was a domestic relationship with the appellants for a brief period of only 2.5 years i.e. from 2008 to 2010.
Thereafter, they never lived together.

The marriage between respondent and Satish Garg was solemnized in 2008 while the complaint was filed in 2021 i.e. after a period of almost 13 years from the date of her marriage alleging acts of domestic violence since her marriage.
Hence, there is a gross delay in filing a complaint alleging domestic violence.
The allegations in the DIR dated 28.08.2021 against the appellants are unsubstantiated and are not supported by any cogent evidence and documents.

Hence, the DIR is devoid of corroborative evidence to substantiate the allegations and the complaint under the DV Act against the appellants is a counterblast to Divorce proceedings between the respondent and her husband Satish Garg and complaint has been falsely filed to use as a pressure tactics to secure illegal gains from the appellants and is abuse of process of KUMAR by KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT 17:39:36 Date: 2024.11.12 +0530 law.
5.

The appellants are senior citizens with multiple health problems and father-in-law can barely walk and needs assistance and mother-in-law is bed-ridden and dependent on others to do daily chores and it has become a general tendency to implicate all the members of husband's family in false cases whenever there is a matrimonial dispute between the parties and Hon'ble Apex Court have termed it as " legal terrorism".

It is also argued that the summoning order passed by Ld. MM is bad in law as there is no offence of domestic violence being committed by the appellants as they used to reside separately from the complainant and the delay of filing the complaint is not explained.
It is submitted that the documents of Ghaziabad Court filed by the respondent do not show that complainant was residing with appellants and domestic relationship in 2021.

Counsel for the respondent has argued that application u/s 5 of Limitation Act should not be allowed and opposed strongly and stated that the present appeal was filed after the delay of 126 days and no sufficient cause of delay has been explained and all the contents of the application are denied and that appellant has mislead the Court by stating completely Digitally signed by KUMAR KUMAR RAJAT Date:
RAJAT 2024.11.12 17:39:41 +0530 baseless and vague averments.

Ld. Counsel has highlighted the various orders filed with the documents in the present appeal that they had engaged various counsels, who has challenged the orders of Ld. Trial Court in different courts, even just after the impugned order, whose copy was supplied to them and it is mentioned in one of the order-sheets of the Ld. Trial Court record and present application and appeal have been filed to harass the respondent.
7. It is further submitted by Ld. Counsel for the complainant/respondent that the order of Ld. Trial Court is just, proper and judicious one and it was passed after considering all the materials including the DIR filed before the Court.
The appellants and their family members including the husband of complainant had harassed her in her matrimonial home and committed various acts of domestic violence.

The complainant was a house wife and she was residing with her husband and the appellants and all the arguments tendered by the appellants are not the part of pleadings in the appeal or before the Ld. Trial Court and in their pleading in the appeal, it is mentioned that domestic relations between respondent and appellants ended in 2016, which is contrary to their claim that it ended in 2010.
Further, there is no limitation prescribed for filing the complaint u/s 12 of the DV Act.

The complainant was residing at C-501, Apex Green Valley Society, Sector 9, Vaishali,
Ghaziabad, UP and her husband had taken loan of Rs. 77 lacs from M/s. Aditya Birla Finance Ltd.,
and after paying some installments, he defaulted later on willfully so that the said financial institution shall take the possession of said house from the complainant and Digitally signed by KUMAR KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT

Date:
2024.11.12 17:39:48 +0530 on 25.06.2022, Ld. MM passed an order that in case the complainant is dispossessed husband would be liable to provide alternate accommodation.

It is also submitted that one appeal was filed by the appellant before the Sessions Court and vide its order dated 20.08.2022, husband was directed to pay the EMI of said loan, which was challenged by husband in the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi, but vide order dated 07.09.2022, the application of her husband was dismissed.

sentences.text: In another order dated 14.02.2023 of the Ld. Sessions Court, it was observed that Domestic Incident Report dated 28.08.2021 was filed before the Ld. Trial Court and the husband was summoned on 26.07.2021 and the summoning of other respondents was kept in abeyance after the consideration of DIR in which there are allegations against the husband and other respondents including appellants and Ld.

Trial was directed to consider the issue of summoning the other respondents after considering the DIR filed in 2021 and one of the appellants Lalita Garg filed a revision petition before the Sessions Court against the order of Ld. Trial Court directing her to pay EMI of the loan taken of the shared house-hold from Aditya Birla Financing Institution, which was jointly owned by her and her son Satish Garg, who is husband of complainant and the said revision was dismissed vide order dated 25.03.2023 and cost of Rs. 50,000/- was imposed on them.

Ld. 
Counsel for the respondent has also argued that the appellants were residing with the complainant under same roof till 2021 and appellant Lalita Garg has filed one petition before Ghaziabad Court against the complainant and her family members under DV Act on false averments to harass and KUMAR RAJAT

Date:
RAJAT 2024.11.12 17:39:54 +0530 humiliate her and her family members and she has alleged that on 15.02.2021, the complainant had beaten her and misbehaved and assaulted appellant's (no. 2) husband.
9.
I have heard the rival contentions and perused the record.

10. As regards the contention of appellants in the application u/s 5 of the Limitation Act that due to the lack of legal knowledge and the fact that previous counsel did not tell them about the fact that impugned order was an appealable order, due to which they could not challenge the said order, it is settled law that ignorance of law is no excuse.

However, considering the fact that the appellants are senior citizens and were not aware of legal nuances and in the judgment of Collector (Supra),
Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that refusing to condone the delay can result in meritorious matter being thrown out at the very threshold and 'every day's delay must be explained' does not mean that a pedantic approach should be adopted and when substantial justice and technical considerations are pitted against each other, the former deserves to be preferred and ordinarily a litigant does not stand to benefit by filing late appeals.

In Rafiq (Supra), it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that contesting parties should not suffer due to lapse on part of their counsel and in N Balakrishnan (Supra), it was held that sufficient cause should be construed liberally and delay of 883 days was condoned.
The appellants filed various revisions/appeals after the passage of impugned order, but the Court is of the opinion that the issues raised by the appellants have to be heard on merits KUMAR
by KUMAR
RAJAT RAJAT 17:40:00 Date: 2024.11.12 +0530 and it is settled law that the Court has to take pragmatic approach while deciding the application u/s 5 of Limitation Act.
There is not much inordinate delay in filing the appeal, which is 126 days.
Considering the above and the judgments cited by the appellants, the application for condonation of delay is allowed and delay of 126 days is condoned in filing the present appeal.

sentences.text: The appellants are the father-in-law and mother-in- law of the respondent.
The marriage between the complainant and her husband Satish Garg was solemnized on 22.04.2008 at Ghaziabad, UP and complainant came to her matrimonial home at R4-B, Dishad Garden, Delhi.

As per Section 2(f) of DV Act: "Domestic relationship"
means a relationship between two persons who live or have, any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage, adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.
12.
The domestic violence is defined in Section 3 of the DV Act and includes physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse.

13. As per Section 2(f), if at any point of time, two persons have lived together in shared house-hold and related through relationship in marriage or are family members living together as a joint family are set to be in domestic relationship and shared house-hold is defined in Section 2(s) that "shared household", means a household where the person aggrieved lives or at any stage has lived in a domestic relationship either singly or along with the respondent and includes such a household whether owned or tenanted either jointly by the aggrieved person and the respondent, or owned or tenanted by either of them in respect of which either the aggrieved person or the Digitally signed by KUMAR KUMAR Date:
RAJAT RAJAT 2024.11.12 17:40:05 +0530 respondent or both jointly or singly have any right, title, interest or equity and includes such a household which may belong to the joint family of which the respondent is a member, irrespective of whether the respondent or the aggrieved person has any right, title or interest in the share household.

14. As per averment in the appeal, the domestic relationship between complainant and appellants ended in 2016, but as per the oral arguments it ended in 2010 and in both there is admission on part of the appellants that they had resided in domestic relationship with the respondent/complainant.
15. As per the Domestic Incident Report, the parents of the complainant had spent huge amount of money in the marriage as per their capacity including gold jewellery, house-hold articles, cash etc.

and after 4-5 days of marriage, appellant Lalita Garg asked complainant to hand over all gold/silver jewellery, cash, gifts to her and she handed over her stridhan to the said appellant and complainant lived with the appellants after the marriage and they used to taunt her for bringing insufficient dowry from her parental house and the complainant was not allowed by the appellants to call her parents and did not provide her proper diet and medical care during her pregnancy and did not allow her to go to her parental house easily on the occasion of festivals and after birth of female child

, the complainant wanted to arrange family functions, but appellants were not willing and they told the complainant that "Ladki ka function koun karta hai", but somehow complainant arranged the function and appellant Lalita Garg taunted her on the point
that her parents/family members Naresh Kumar Garg vs Shikha Garg on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55800544/

All the gifts are stridhan of the married woman and she is entitled for the same.

16. As per DIR, there are lot of allegations of misbehavior by the appellants and the cruelty by way of neglecting herself and treat her like a maid and whenever her brother used to visit her matrimonial house, appellants taunted her brother by finding fault in the complainant and on 14.10.2010,
appellants along with her husband shifted to C-501, Apex Green Valley, Vaishali Sector 9, Ghaziabad with complainant and minor children and male child was born on 02.10.2011 and on the occasion of Chuchak, the appellants pressurized the parents of complainant to gift sweets, jewellery, gifts, cash etc. to whole family and appellant Lalita had shouted at the husband of complainant whenever he gifted something to the complainant and appellant Naresh Kumar Garg used to instigate her husband against the complainant.
The complainant was also harassed with regard to the movable and immovable properties.
The appellants always tried to keep complainant away from her husband and her husband was having relationship with some other woman and her stridhan was also kept by the appellants.

The appellants and her husband had not paid any money for day to day expenses to the complainant and her minor children and she lodged complaint against them and appellants along with their son had committed fraud with the complainant and deliberately stopped paying monthly installments of Flat No. C-501, Apex Green Valley, Vaishali Sector 9, Ghaziabad, UP.
KUMAR by KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT

Ld. Trial Court had passed an order and specifically mentioned that there are allegations against the appellants that they had demanded the dowry from the complainant and taunted her for not bringing enough dowry and there are specific allegations against appellant no. 2 in the petition before the Ld. Trial Court for taunting the complainant and she was also taunted for giving birth to a female child and gold tagdi of complainant gifted by the appellants was taken from her by them and also appellant had taken the stridhan of respondent/complainant.

18. As regards the limitation argued by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant that the DV petition was filed with delay and summoning was done with great delay, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kamatchi Vs. Laxmi Narayanan AIR 2022 SC 2932 that the provisions of DV Act contemplate filing of an application u/s 12 to initiate the proceedings before the concerned Magistrate.

sentences.text: After hearing both sides and after taking into account, the material on record, the Magistrate may pass an appropriate order u/s 12 of the DV Act.
It is only the breach of such order which constitutes an offence as is clear from Section 31 of the Act.
Thus, if there be any offence committed in terms of the provisions of the Act, the limitation prescribed u/s 468 of Cr.P.C. will apply from the date of commission of offence.

By the time an application is preferred u/s 12 DV Act, there is no offence committed in terms of the provisions of the Act and as such there would never be a starting point for limitation from the date of application u/s 12 DV Act and it will arise only when there is breach of Naresh Kumar Garg vs Shikha Garg on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55800544/
6 any order passed u/s 12 of the Act.

sentences.text: KUMAR RAJAT RAJAT

From the perusal of the DIR as well as complaint of the complainant there are allegations of humiliation, taunting, keeping of stridhan of complainant, causing cruelty and harassment levelled against the appellants by the complainant.
Ld. Counsel for complainant has also highlighted the orders of revisional/appellate courts wherein no relief was granted to the appellants.
Order of Ghaziabad Court shows that the appellants and respondent are not disconnected till 2021.

The judgments cited by Ld. Counsel for the appellants are not applicable to the facts of the present case as in those judgments of Sushil Kumar Sharma (Supra)
and Savitri Devi (Supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court had dealt with the provisions of Section 498A/406 IPC and the provisions of DV Act are entirely different and they are brought to safeguard the women from being the victims of domestic violence and to prevent domestic violence in the society.

CONCLUSION 20. Considering the DIR as well as the complaint u/s 12 of the DV Act, wherein specific allegations have been made against the appellants by the respondent/complainant, the order of Ld. Trial Court does not appear to be without any application of mind and it was passed after considering the said material and the specific allegations against the appellants and they were summoned accordingly and
as such the said order dated 20.02.2023 does not suffer from any material illegality and as such does not need any interference from this Court.
21. Hence, the appeal of the appellants, being devoid of merits, is hereby dismissed and disposed of accordingly.
